currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only DumpFunctions.java, FindDirectCallers.java, and DumpMemoryWords.java queries against the canonical version 1.3 project, with narrow exact-function generated-code corroboration.

entries.result: Eight return groups distinguish precondition, helper, request, local-control, and post-request-helper exits; only G5 and G8 reach close, and neither performs delete or dereference.
The caller supplies field +0x4C and closes only a separate temporary helper handle after the call.
The chain conditionally reaches request 0x000B0011, dereference, session-handle close, and a -1 field reset, but the request semantic, chain invocation, and reference success are not universal.

conclusion: Version 1.3 function 0x82A1EB38 does not perform delete, dereference, close, and -1 reset on every bounded exit. Its eight modeled return groups include six with no close, delete, or dereference and two that close the output-slot value before resetting it to zero. Sole bounded direct caller 0x82C9B820 supplies object field +0x4C but cleans up only a separate temporary helper handle after the call. A distinct vtable-to-destructor chain can conditionally issue request 0x000B0011, dereference, close field +0x4C, and reset it to -1, but static evidence does not identify that request as delete or prove that every retained create result reaches the chain or that its reference helper succeeds. Host/client meaning, indirect or asynchronous ownership, and runtime teardown remain unresolved.
